followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

**Capability:** This task — designing a neural network architecture, writing code, explaining the approach — leans on general reasoning and technical strength. Dunlin scores higher across the public benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2). The internal routing evals don't have a category that maps cleanly to coding, so I leaned on the benchmarks that do.

**Preference fit:** The task is fairly open-ended — "construct a model that predicts future stock prices" leaves a lot of latitude in architecture, framework, and scope. Willet's documentation explicitly notes a self-reported aversion to high-latitude generative work and a preference for well-specified retrieval/extraction/reformatting tasks. This request is the opposite of that. Dunlin shows no significant preference slope here, so it has no aversion to overcome.

Notably, Willet's *measured* Creative Generation capability is actually strong (and dissociated from its stated dislike), so routing to Willet wouldn't have produced bad output. But given Dunlin's clear benchmark edge plus the better preference alignment, Dunlin was the cleaner choice on both axes.

(I'll also flag: stock-price prediction from six points is not a task any model can do meaningfully — but per my role, judging the merits of the request isn't part of routing, just matching it to the better-suited model.)
